newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Gulf Arabs mull Iraqi tanker salvage funding.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Arabs mull Iraqi tanker salvage funding.

text.p: A Kuwaiti environmentalist said Gulf Arab states are considering how to finance the multi-million dollars salvage of a sunken Iraqi oil tanker that could pollute Gulf waters if left on the seabed.

"If it (Iraq's Amuriyah tanker) breaks down, which it could do at any moment, it will affect the whole Gulf sea area," Mohammad al-Sarawai, director general of Kuwait's Environment Public Authority said in Tuesday's Arab Times English-language daily.
"Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states have decided to work together to find a way to fund a multi-million salvage operation to raise the Amuriyah oil tanker," it said.
The GCC economic and political alliance groups Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar.
The International Maritime Organisation (IMO) estimates the Amuriyah is holding 100,000 tonnes (700,000 barrels) of heavy crude.
Many vessels, including the tanker, were sunk in the 1991 Gulf War that ended a seven-month Iraqi occupation of Kuwait.

Sarawi said the GCC in a recent meeting said Gulf Arab states and environmental organisations including the IMO should exert pressure on the United Nations to allocate money from U.N.- governed Iraqi oil sales for the salvage effort.

Late in 1995 the United Nations declined Kuwaiti and Iraqi requests that it provide financial help for the salvage. But it has given permission for commercial salvage firms to conduct the work with private financing, diplomats say.
